chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them)...
...regarding the slave: if he kills a free man, he is handed over to the guardians of the killed one; so if they desire, they kill him, and if they desire, they enslave him.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal consequence for a slave who kills a free person according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'diya' (blood money) and retribution (qisas) in cases where a slave kills a free man, granting the victim's heirs the discretion to choose between execution or manumission into slavery. It reflects the classical Shia juristic view on the valuation of life based on social status, where the slave's life is often considered equivalent to that of a free woman or a specific portion of a free man's diya, allowing heirs to absorb the slave into their household as compensation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>)

regarding the slave when he kills the free, he would be handed over to the guardians of the killed one, so if they so desire to, they kill him, and if they so desire to they keep him (as a slave for them)’.
